name: Congenital Myasthenic Syndromes Due to Defective Axonal Transport
aliases: Congenital Myasthenic Syndrome Axonal Transport Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Myasthenic Syndromes

criteria.description: Presence of early-onset fatigable muscle weakness with ptosis and ophthalmoplegia
Electromyography showing decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes affecting axonal transport (e.g., DOK7, RAPSN, or related genes)
Improvement of symptoms with acetylcholinesterase inhibitors or other CMS-specific therapies
Muscle biopsy showing postsynaptic abnormalities or reduced acetylcholine receptor density

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical presentation plus electrophysiological evidence and confirmation by genetic testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of autoimmune myasthenia gravis and other neuromuscular junction disorders.

searchTerms: weak eye muscles that worsen with activity
muscle weakness that worsens with use

common.symptomName: Respiratory muscle weakness with exertional dyspnea
Mild scoliosis secondary to muscle weakness
searchTerms: mild spine curvature from muscle weakness
early scoliosis due to weak muscles

occasional.symptomName: Dysphagia due to pharyngeal muscle involvement
searchTerms: difficulty swallowing from throat muscle weakness
swallowing problems due to muscle involvement
slight loss of muscle bulk in arms or legs
eyelid droop that gets worse when cold

rare.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias secondary to autonomic involvement
searchTerms: heart rhythm issues due to autonomic dysfunction
cardiac arrhythmias related to nerve involvement

rare.symptomName: Cognitive impairment due to hypoxic episodes
searchTerms: memory and thinking problems from low oxygen
brain fog due to lack of oxygen

laboratory: Normal autoimmune antibody panel (negative anti-AChR and anti-MuSK antibodies)
imaging: Muscle MRI may show selective muscle involvement
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes involved in axonal transport and neuromuscular junction function (e.g., DOK7, RAPSN, GFPT1)
other: Electrophysiological studies showing decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation

distinguishingFeatures: Proximal muscle weakness improving with activity

redFlags: Severe bulbar weakness with aspiration risk
Lack of response to acetylcholinesterase inhibitors
